Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + capacity uplift — legal redlines needed

Ben — thanks for the heads up. Quick reads / proposed moves:

1) SLA credits: remove the unilateral "service credit cap" language that limits credits to a single incident. Replace with the attached proposed SLA table that preserves our SLOs but provides clearer credit calculation tied to consecutive days of breach.

2) Data retention: add explicit carve-out permitting short-term K/V caching for model performance but preserve customer data isolation commitments. Proposed language attached in-line below.

3) Auto-renew: accept Skyline's preference for explicit renewal; propose option to add a 90-day renewal notice window with pricing re-opener if usage increases >25%.

I will prepare a tracked redline of the Order Form and draft "Exhibit X — Burst Credits" that defines pre-purchase blocks, expiration (12 months), and conversion to overage at defined rates. If Procurement pushes hard on keeping the SLA credit table as-is, we'll surface that as a negotiation point rather than a legal blocker.

Lauren Bishop | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com | +1 650-555-0233

Hi Samira / Rajiv — attaching the tracked redline (Skyline_Redline_v3.docx) and a short Exhibit that defines burst credits and expiry. Summary of changes:

- Converted to 24-month term starting 2028-01-01 (clean line item).
- Added Exhibit X that defines burst credits (pre-purchase blocks, 12-month expiry) and conversion rates for overage.
- Reworked SLA credits language per legal suggestion; call-out where we can be flexible.
- Removed auto-renew; added 90-day notice with pricing re-opener if usage increases >25%.

As next steps: please confirm whether Skyline will accept Exhibit X as pre-purchased burst blocks or insist on open overage billing. We can make Exhibit optional (customer choice) to speed signature.

If you want to run through the legal edits, Lauren and I can join a 30-min call Monday.

Thanks,
Ben
